description: A large, evergreen tree with a spreading crown and drooping branches. It is highly revered in traditional Ayurvedic medicine, particularly for its heart-healing properties.
characteristics: Distinctive smooth, grey bark that flakes off in large, flat pieces, leaving a pale, scarred trunk beneath.
habitat: Thrives in well-drained, moist soils, often found along riverbanks and dry riverbeds.
distribution: Found extensively across Bangladesh, frequently planted along avenues and in botanical gardens.
benefits: The bark is a powerful cardiovascular tonic. The tree also provides excellent shade and acts as a host for the Tasar silkworm.
uses: Bark is dried and boiled as a medicinal tea for heart ailments. The wood is extremely hard and used for boat building and agricultural implements.

fruitInfo.name: Arjun Fruit (অর্জুন ফল)
fruitInfo.description: A woody, fibrous, star-shaped fruit with five prominent wings.
fruitInfo.uses: Used in some traditional medicinal preparations, though the bark is much more commonly used.

flowerInfo.name: Arjun Flower
flowerInfo.description: Small, cup-shaped flowers occurring in auxiliary spikes, carrying a strong fragrance.

description: A large deciduous tree known for its highly medicinal fruit. It is one of the three crucial ingredients in the famous Ayurvedic herbal remedy, 'Triphala'.
characteristics: Tall, straight trunk with a broad, rounded canopy and large, broadly oval leaves clustered at the ends of branches.
habitat: Tropical and subtropical forests, preferring moist valleys.
distribution: Grows wild in the deciduous forests of Bangladesh, including the Chittagong Hill Tracts and Madhupur tract.
benefits: Fruit is highly beneficial for digestive health, respiratory ailments, and immunity.
uses: Dried fruits are ground into powder for medicinal use (Triphala). The wood is used for packing cases and low-cost furniture.

fruitInfo.name: Bahera (বহেরা)
fruitInfo.description: A somewhat rounded, grey-velvety drupe containing a single hard stone.
fruitInfo.uses: Dried and used extensively in Ayurvedic and Unani medicine.

flowerInfo.name: Bahera Flower
flowerInfo.description: Small flowers with a strong, sometimes unpleasant odor, arranged in solitary, auxiliary spikes.

description: A small to medium-sized deciduous tree famous for bearing round, highly nutritious fruits. It is another core component of the 'Triphala' formulation.
characteristics: Crooked trunk with spreading branches and feathery, light-green pinnate leaves.
habitat: Tropical and subtropical climates, highly adaptable to dry and degraded soils.
distribution: Widespread across Bangladesh in both wild and cultivated forms, often planted in homesteads.
benefits: One of the richest natural sources of Vitamin C. Boosts immunity, improves hair health, and acts as a powerful antioxidant.
uses: Fruit is eaten raw, pickled, candied, or powdered. Oil extracted from the fruit is widely used in hair care.

fruitInfo.name: Amla (আমলকি)
fruitInfo.description: Spherical, light greenish-yellow fruit with a smooth and hard appearance, featuring six vertical stripes.
fruitInfo.taste: Sour, bitter, and astringent, famously leaving a sweet aftertaste when water is drunk afterward
fruitInfo.uses: Eaten raw with salt, made into achaar (pickle), morobba (candied), and dried for medicine.

flowerInfo.name: Amla Flower
flowerInfo.description: Tiny, inconspicuous flowers appearing in clusters along the branchlets.

description: A medium to large deciduous tree known in Ayurveda as the 'King of Medicines'. It is the final ingredient in the 'Triphala' triad.
characteristics: Dark brown bark with deep longitudinal cracks and thick, leathery, oval-shaped leaves.
habitat: Dry to moist deciduous forests, tolerating a variety of soil conditions.
distribution: Found in the hill tracts and sal forests of Bangladesh, as well as cultivated in medicinal gardens.
benefits: Highly valued for digestive aid, detoxification, and anti-inflammatory properties.
uses: Fruit is dried and powdered for medicinal use. Historically used in tanning leather due to high tannin content.

fruitInfo.name: Haritaki (হরিতকি)
fruitInfo.description: Oval or elliptical drupe that turns yellowish-brown to blackish when ripe and dried, heavily ribbed.
fruitInfo.uses: Dried, powdered, and consumed with warm water for digestive health; used in Triphala.

flowerInfo.name: Haritaki Flower
flowerInfo.description: Small, star-shaped flowers that bloom in terminal spikes, emitting a strong, unpleasant scent.

description: A massive, long-lived, evergreen tree that produces pod-like fruit containing an edible, highly acidic pulp. Though botanically native to Africa, it has been deeply embedded in South Asian cuisine for millennia.
characteristics: Huge, dense, umbrella-shaped canopy with delicate, feathery pinnate leaves and a stout, heavily fissured trunk.
habitat: Tropical and subtropical regions, highly drought-resistant and tolerant of poor soils.
distribution: Cultivated and grows wild abundantly throughout rural and urban Bangladesh.
benefits: Provides dense shade. Fruit is rich in tartaric acid, B vitamins, and essential minerals.
uses: Fruit pulp is a staple souring agent in curries, chutneys, and street food (like Fuchka). Wood is very hard, used for chopping blocks and furniture.

fruitInfo.name: Tamarind (তেঁতুল)
fruitInfo.description: A brown, pod-like legume containing sticky pulp and hard, glossy black seeds.
fruitInfo.taste: Intensely sour when green, becoming sweeter but remaining tart when ripe
fruitInfo.uses: Essential in South Asian cooking, chutneys, Fuchka/Chotpoti water, and cooling summer drinks.

flowerInfo.name: Tamarind Flower
flowerInfo.description: Small, delicate, orchid-like flowers growing in drooping racemes.
